sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: AP-TGFα shedding assay in HEK293FT cells; FLAG-tagged zebrafish LPA6 was expressed at the cell surface and activated the AP-TGFα shedding pathway, demonstrating surface expression and receptor function were preserved.
sites.rationale: The topology landmarks place LPAR6 residues 1–18 as extracellular with no signal peptide, making the N-terminus the only extracellular terminus available for a surface tag. L6 reports a FLAG epitope (a short ~8 aa tag) placed between an HA signal sequence and the start of zebrafish LPA6 (residues 1–312); after signal-peptide cleavage the FLAG is extracellular and the receptor is functional in a GPCR activation assay. Because no specific residue of the zebrafish or human sequence is named as the junction, the position is topology-derived: insert_after_residue = 0 (prepend before M1), residue_after = M. L2 independently confirms that full-length human LPAR6 tolerates a large N-terminal domain insertion (BRIL) at the same position, strengthening confidence in this site. Full-length zebrafish LPA6 (residues 1–312, ortholog of human LPAR6) was expressed in HEK293FT cells with an N-terminal haemagglutinin signal sequence followed by a FLAG epitope tag; after HA-SP cleavage the FLAG is presented at the extracellular face. Human LPAR6 has no annotated signal peptide and its N-terminus (residues 1–18) is extracellular, so the equivalent junction is a prepend before M1 (insert_after_residue = 0). L2 independently corroborates: full-length human LPAR6 in pFastBac carries an HA signal peptide and a BRIL domain at its N-terminus, confirming the extracellular N-terminus tolerates a large domain insertion in the same protein.

sources.claim: A modified pEGFPC1 vector (Clontech) encoding the wild-type or a mutant LPA 6 , consisting of a haemagglutinin signal sequence, FLAG epitope tag and zebrafish LPA 6 (residues 1–312) [ 5 ], was transfected together with a pCAGGS plasmid encoding alkaline phosphatase (AP)-tagged TGFα (AP-TGFα; human codon-optimized) into HEK293FT cells (seeded 1-day before the transfection in 4 ml per 6-cm culture dish at a cell concentration of 2 x 10 5 cells/ml) by using a polyethylenimine (PEI) transfection reagent (400 ng LPA 6 plasmid, 1 μg AP-TGFα plasmid

literature_notes: Six ledger lines were evaluated. L6 (zebrafish LPA6 ortholog, FLAG, functional assay) and L2 (human LPAR6, BRIL domain, structural construct) both pin the extracellular N-terminal prepend position (insert_after_residue = 0); because they converge on the same junction, one site is reported, grounded in L6 (better functional validation and short-epitope tag). L2 is noted as corroborating evidence in the rationale. L1 and L4 describe GFP fused to the C-terminus of full-length human LPAR6; the C-terminus falls in the intracellular region (295–344) and is therefore not a surface-tag site. L3 and L5 describe LgBiT replacing C-terminal residues F325–A344, also within the intracellular region (295–344). No ledger line supports an insertion in any of the three short extracellular loops (ECL1: 76–86, ECL2: 155–179, ECL3: 253–271).

literature_other_positions.note: GFP fused to the C-terminus of full-length human LPAR6 (pcDNA3-LPAR6-TEV-GFP-H8); the C-terminus lies in the intracellular region (295–344), so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.

C-terminal residues F325–A344 of LPAR6 were replaced with LgBiT for NanoBiT-based G-protein complex assembly; residue 325 is within the intracellular C-terminal region (295–344), making this an intracellular modification.
